Overflown
OH-ver-flohn
v. (archaic past part. of OVERFLOW)
Anglo-Saxon ofer (over) + flowan (to flow) — the older strong past participle of overflow, displaced in modern English by overflowed but retained in the Authorized Version.

Biblical Definition

When it had overflown all his banks. Whose foundation was overflown with a flood. With the arms of a flood shall they be overflown.

Overflown gathers three very different floods under one word. The mighty men who cross the Jordan to David at Ziklag do so when it had overflown all his banks — the river at full spring spate, a natural obstacle their loyalty refuses to be stopped by. Job's friend Eliphaz uses the same word for the wicked, whose foundation was overflown with a flood, God's judgment pictured as an inundation that sweeps away everything a man has built his life on. Daniel's vision applies it a third way, to an invading army: with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown, the language of a river turned into the language of war. Scripture's overflown moves, in three verses, from a literal river crossed by the faithful, to a metaphorical flood of judgment on the wicked, to a flood of armies sweeping over nations — one word carrying nature, judgment, and history at once.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828), from OVERFLOW: to flow over; to cover with water or other fluid, as land not usually covered; the older strong participle, now largely replaced by overflowed.

expand to see more

OVERFLOW, v.t. To spread over; to cover with water or other fluid.

OVERFLOW, v.i. To run over, as a stream or vessel; to be superabundant.

OVERFLOWN, the older strong past participle, as flown from fly, now largely displaced by overflowed.

Applied literally to the Jordan at flood stage, and figuratively to judgment and invasion.

The imagery of an overflowing flood is a standing biblical figure for sudden, sweeping judgment.

Key Scripture

1Ch 12:15 — "These are they that went over Jordan in the first month, when it had overflown all his banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east, and toward the west."

Job 22:16 — "Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:"

Dan 11:22 — "And with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant."

Modern Corruption

Treating the Jordan crossing in 1 Chronicles 12 as mere adventure-narrative color, rather than as evidence entered for the mighty men's covenant loyalty to David, misses why the Chronicler bothers to mention the river's condition at all.

expand to see more

A purely literary reading of 1 Chronicles 12 can pass over when it had overflown all his banks as incidental scene-setting. The Chronicler's own purpose is theological: these are men counted worthy of remembrance precisely because they came to David through danger, at flood stage, when a lesser loyalty would have waited for the water to fall.

Beyond the point above, this entry faces no further significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that Scripture's floods are never merely meteorological — the same word that describes a river at spring spate describes the LORD's judgment sweeping over the wicked and armies sweeping over nations, one figure doing triple duty across the canon.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Overflown preserves the older strong past participle pattern seen in flown, grown, and known, a form English has since regularized toward the weak -ed ending in most verbs but the Authorized Version retains throughout.

expand to see more

Overflown in 1 Chronicles 12 describes the Jordan at full spring flood, crossed by David's mighty men.

Overflown in Job 22 pictures a wicked man's whole foundation swept away by judgment.

Overflown in Daniel 11 turns the same flood-image into a figure for an invading army.

In every case the word marks a force too great to be resisted by ordinary means.

The strong participle form (rather than overflowed) is characteristic of the Authorized Version's older English.

Usage

"When it had overflown all his banks — the Jordan at flood, crossed by David's loyal mighty men."

"Whose foundation was overflown with a flood — judgment pictured as an inundation on the wicked."

"With the arms of a flood shall they be overflown — an invading army as a sweeping flood."
